title: The Sticky Auction Receipts
story: Going once, going twice: four antique clocks sold at the St. Brendan's autumn auction, each made in a different year from a different wood, and each to a different buyer. Hattie wrote a receipt for every sale, then set her mug of hot cider down on the stack. The receipts are now one sticky brick. Can you match each buyer to a clock, a wood, and a year?

texts: Of the buyer whose clock dates from 1880 and the buyer whose clock dates from 1890, one is Della and the other is Otis.
Otis bought a newer clock than the buyer of the mantel clock did.
The buyer of the cuckoo clock is neither Otis nor Della.
The buyer whose clock is oak bought a clock exactly 30 years newer than the buyer whose clock is walnut did.
Of Otis and Carmen, one bought a clock made of cherry and the other bought a clock made of maple.
Otis bought a clock exactly 20 years older than the buyer of the banjo clock did.
The buyer whose clock is maple bought a clock a decade newer than the buyer whose clock is cherry did.

trace.text: Clue 3 gives an X.
Clue 2 means the mantel clock cannot be 1910 and Otis cannot be 1880.
Clue 4 means oak cannot be 1880, 1890, or 1900 and walnut cannot be 1890, 1900, or 1910.
Oak must go with 1910: clue 4 rules out 1880, 1890, and 1900.
Walnut must go with 1880: clue 4 rules out 1890, 1900, and 1910.
Otis must go with the ship's clock: clue 2 rules out the mantel clock; clue 3 rules out the cuckoo clock; clue 6 rules out the banjo clock.
Since Otis can still be only 1890, 1900, or 1910, clue 6 means the banjo clock cannot be 1880, 1890, or 1900 and Otis cannot be 1900 or 1910.
Otis must go with 1890: clue 2 rules out 1880; clue 6 rules out 1900 and 1910.
The banjo clock must go with 1910: clue 6 rules out 1880, 1890, and 1900.
Oak goes with 1910, so oak also goes with the banjo clock.
The ship's clock goes with Otis, so the ship's clock also goes with 1890.
Since the mantel clock can still be only 1880 or 1900 and Otis can still be only 1890, clue 2 means the mantel clock cannot be 1900.
The mantel clock must go with 1880: clue 2 rules out 1900 and 1910; 1890 already goes with the ship's clock.
The cuckoo clock must go with 1900: the other choices are already taken.
Walnut goes with 1880, so walnut also goes with the mantel clock.
Since maple can still be only 1890 or 1900 and cherry can still be only 1890 or 1900, clue 7 means maple cannot be 1890 and cherry cannot be 1900.
Cherry must go with 1890: clue 7 rules out 1900; the other choices are already taken.
Maple must go with 1900: clue 7 rules out 1890; the other choices are already taken.
Otis goes with 1890, so Otis also goes with cherry.
The ship's clock goes with Otis, so the ship's clock also goes with cherry.
The cuckoo clock must go with maple: oak is already ruled out for 1910; the other choices are already taken.
Clue 1 limits the choices (mark the X's it gives).
Della must go with 1880: clue 1 rules out 1910; 1900 is already ruled out for the cuckoo clock; 1890 already goes with Otis.
Della must go with walnut: oak is already ruled out for 1910; maple is already ruled out for 1900; cherry already goes with Otis.
Della must go with the mantel clock: clue 3 rules out the cuckoo clock; the banjo clock is already ruled out for 1910; the ship's clock already goes with Otis.
Clue 5 limits the choices (mark the X's it gives).
Carmen must go with maple: clue 5 rules out oak; the other choices are already taken.
Pablo must go with oak: clue 5 rules out maple; the other choices are already taken.
